name: Creality Falcon T1 5W UV
tagline: 5W UV galvo module: glass, film, and sensitive plastics on the T1 chassis
tldr: The 5W UV WaveSync module targets materials diode and fiber struggle with: glass, some films, and heat-sensitive plastics. Install on the same Falcon T1 enclosure when your shop adds UV jobs after wood or metal modules.
mainObjective: UV galvo marking for glass and specialty plastics on the T1 platform

priceRange.note: Official Creality store, Oct 2026: $3,999, complete machine

pros: Marks glass, crystal and clear acrylic, which diode and fiber lasers handle poorly
Smallest spot of the T1 modules (0.014 mm in CNX Software's spec table)
Internal-engraving lens and bracket included, per Creality
cons: Marking only: it does not cut
Not Class 1 in open-cover modes (conveyor, rotary): eye protection is needed then
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W SKU on Creality Falcon T1 UV. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run glass test tiles at low power: UV on glass is unforgiving. Keep dedicated ventilation practices for UV fumes per Creality guidance.
primaryUse: 5W UV galvo module for glass and specialty marking on the Creality Falcon T1 chassis.

moduleSystem.headline: WaveSync swappable galvo modules
moduleSystem.description: One enclosed T1 chassis accepts Creality diode (20W/40W), fiber (20W), MOPA (60W), and UV (5W) modules: install one head at a time.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 5W UV module covers glass and heat-sensitive plastics on the T1 chassis: niche work that diode and fiber modules cannot do on the same platform.
editorialDepth.limitations: Specialty module with narrow material list. Requires chassis and swap discipline. Not a first purchase for most shops: compare the base diode profile unless UV jobs are already sold.

faq.question: What is the T1 UV module for?
faq.answer: Cold marking on materials that burn, melt or reflect other lasers: glass, crystal, clear acrylic, many plastics and some films. CNX Software's spec table lists a 0.014 mm spot. A fine mark on a 10 × 10 cm glass panel took about 5–10 min in our benchmark.

faq.question: Can the T1 UV engrave inside glass or crystal?
faq.answer: Creality ships the UV version with an internal-engraving F-theta lens and bracket, intended for subsurface marks in crystal. Expect to test settings carefully: results depend on the quality of the blank.

faq.question: How much is the UV module compared with other T1 options?
faq.answer: $3,999 for the T1 UV bundle, or $2,599 for the module alone, on Creality's US store in October 2026. That is $1,500 more than the entry diode bundle, so it only pays if glass, crystal or plastic marking is a regular product.

standoutFeatures.title: Cold marking
standoutFeatures.body: The UV wavelength marks with little heat, so glass, clear acrylic and heat-sensitive plastics are marked without melting or cracking.

standoutFeatures.title: Inside-crystal engraving kit
standoutFeatures.body: Creality includes an internal-engraving F-theta lens and bracket with the UV version, for subsurface marks in crystal blocks.
